messages:
Alisha (EngPlatform): Deploybot detected p99 latency spike during canary for r-inference v2.3.7 on eu-dedicated pools. Canary paused at 60%. Holding rollout and considering pin to v2.3.6 for affected pools. Need customer-facing status text and statuspage update. ETA decision in ~20m.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused at 2026-06-18T15:12:01Z (60% complete). Metric: p99_token_latency +42% vs baseline. Logs: /var/log/deploys/1787654321.log

Mike (Support): Noted. Which customers will see impact if we keep pinned? Any active SLAs affected?

Alisha (EngPlatform): Immediate surface: EU dedicated customers using >=256 context pools — roughly 8 customers on reserved capacity. Hosted routes will fallback to other regions if routing policy allows. No SLA breach expected for Hosted, but we'll need to notify Dedicated customers proactively.

Santiago (Runtime): Early triage: regression appears related to a kernel selection change in the custom attention kernel for long-context. Quick option: pin docker image + config to previous kernel flag and redeploy targeted pools. That avoids full rollback of model binary.

Priya (PM): For comms: short statuspage update + targeted customer emails to those 8 customers. We should offer a temporary capacity bump or migration guidance. I'll draft language, please iterate.

Alisha (EngPlatform): Draft statuspage snippet — short and factual:

```
Component: EU Dedicated Inference
Status: Degraded performance (partial)
Impact: Some customers on reserved EU GPU pools may experience increased latency for long-context requests; traffic has been routed away from affected canaries.
Update: We paused an ongoing canary rollout (v2.3.7) and pinned affected pools to v2.3.6 while we validate kernel behavior. Engineers are investigating; ETA for next update: 1 hour.
```

Mike (Support): That reads fine. Add an advisory line about contacting success if they see errors, not just latency.

Alisha (EngPlatform): Updated snippet with contact line in the draft below. Also drafting targeted email for the 8 Dedicated customers:

```
Subject: Brief maintenance notice — Temporary performance mitigation in EU dedicated pools

Hi <CustomerName>,

We’re writing to let you know we paused a canary rollout for an inference runtime update (v2.3.7) after observing increased latency for long-context workloads on some EU dedicated GPU pools. To protect your production traffic we have pinned affected pools to the prior runtime (v2.3.6) and routed traffic away from canaries.

What this means for you:
- You may see transient increases in request latency for very long-context calls while we validate a fix.
- No data loss is expected and requests will not be dropped.
- If you rely on strict latency SLAs, we can provision temporary burst capacity or help migrate workloads to alternative pools/regions.

Next steps:
- Engineering is actively investigating the kernel selection regression.
- We expect a follow-up update within 1 hour with either a targeted fix or a scheduled rollback plan.

If you’d like immediate assistance or prefer we schedule a migration, reply to this message or open a support ticket and mention: #1787654321.

Thanks — Alisha on behalf of Redwood Inference Ops
```

Santiago (Runtime): LGTM. Add a short engineering note to the email that this is a performance mitigation (not a security or correctness issue). Helps prevent escalations.

Alisha (EngPlatform): Done. Finalized customer email includes that line. Also prepared internal release note and rollback decision log for audit: "Pin to v2.3.6 for eu-dedicated pools at 2026-06-18T15:14Z; canary paused; monitoring extended."

OpsBot: Action logged: incident-1787654321 created, severity: info, assigned: eng-platform, runtime. Notification: Dedicated customers list queued for targeted email (8 recipients).

Priya (PM): Approving the statuspage + email. Mike please prepare the support playbook snippet (FAQ) to attach to the customer email thread (migration steps + how to request burst capacity).

Mike (Support): On it. I'll drop a 2-step migration snippet in next message and attach to outbound email template.

Alisha (EngPlatform): Thanks all. We're proceeding with pin now. Will update thread when kernel root cause is identified or if we decide to roll forward.

Santiago (Runtime): Quick note for postmortem: collect kernel selection traces + representative requests from canary traffic window.

Mike (Support): Support playbook ready, attaching snippet ->

```
Migration quick steps:
1) Enable eu-fallback routing: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routing/fallback -d '{"region":"eu","target":"us-west"}'`
2) Request burst capacity: open a support ticket with subject "Burst request — incident 1787654321" and include estimated qps.
```

Alisha (EngPlatform): Perfect. Final update: statuspage and email scheduled for immediate dispatch to affected customers. Will post follow-up in 45m or earlier if we have a fix.

Priya (PM): Thanks team. Keep updates concise. I'll own the customer follow-ups and timelines.
